subject: Throughput tier smoothing & credit structure for high-volume hosted API
messages:
From: Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Rate card + credits for forecasted spike

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We did an internal sizing run and expect a big uplift in Q3 as we shift real-time personalization traffic to Redwood. Attached is a short CSV with our expected token profile by endpoint and hour.

Two quick asks: 1) can you share the hosted API rate card that maps token ranges to unit prices, and 2) do you support smoothing or crediting so we don’t get hit by sharp monthly overages in month 1? We’re evaluating both monthly commits and a blended commit + overage approach.

Kirsten
VP, Product — BlueBay Commerce

Attachment: bluebay-usage-projection-q3.csv (CSV, 18KB)

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate card + credits for forecasted spike

Kirsten —

Appreciate the projection — that helps a lot. Attaching our hosted rate card PDF for baseline unit prices and the default slab structure. Quick highlights:
- Baseline (pay-as-you-go): $0.0009 / token for generation on our verified LLM-XL variant.
- 3-tier commit discounts at 1M / 10M / 50M tokens with stepped pricing.
- We offer an optional smoothing mechanism (monthly debit/credit bucket) and limited rollover credits for annual commitments.

Two clarifying Qs before I propose a concrete option: 1) what % of your volume is latency-sensitive (95th p95 < 200ms requirement)? 2) are you open to a 6-month ramped commit (e.g., 25% -> 50% -> 100%)?

I’ve looped in Ben (pricing lead) and Lauren (account lead) to sketch tailored options once we have those answers.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-ratecard-v1.pdf (PDF, 72KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@bluebaycommerce.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate card + credits for forecasted spike

Dylan/Team —

Answers: ~70% of our calls are latency-sensitive (homepage personalization + checkout suggestions). We prefer a predictable monthly bill during the rollout window; a ramped commit is acceptable if you can provide an initial buffer or usage credits to absorb early overshoot.

We would also like clarity on how rounding is done for token buckets and whether partial-month credits prorate. Procurement is copied for T&Cs.

- Samir
Director, Engineering — BlueBay

Cc: procurement@bluebaycommerce.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@bluebaycommerce.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate card + credits for forecasted spike

Samir/Kirsten —

Thanks for the detail. Proposed approaches (summary):

Option A — Ramped commit + buffer credits (recommended):
- 6-month ramp: commit 30% / 60% / 100% across first three months, then steady-state monthly commit.
- We provide a one-time "onboarding credit" equal to 10% of the first-month committed tokens to buffer overshoot.
- Tiered unit prices applied to the committed portion, overages billed at a blended overage rate with step-down at 1.25x committed volume.

Option B — Annual prepay with rollover:
- Prepay N tokens annually at deeper discounts (15–22% depending on band).
- Up to 20% rollover per quarter that can be consumed later in the year.

Operational notes: smoothing uses a rolling 30-day bucket that can move credits forward/back across billing cycles; partial-month prorates on day counts. We also include a dedicated spikes buffer for latency-sensitive endpoints on Dedicated or a higher-tier hosted SLA.

Requesting:
1) Confirmation that the 10% onboarding credit is acceptable for month 1.
2) If Option A, confirm the target committed token bands you want us to model (I can run tokenized-cost sims against your CSV).

I can prepare a clean commercial term sheet once you confirm direction.

-Ben
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@bluebaycommerce.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial term sheet (draft) + next steps

Team —

Following Ben's recommendation, I attached a short draft term sheet that codifies Option A with the ramp schedule and the 10% onboarding credit. Key points:
- Ramp schedule: Month1 30% commit, Month2 60%, Month3+ steady at 100% of the agreed baseline.
- One-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month1 committed tokens.
- Blended overage: 1.25x step-down to a lower overage rate after crossing that threshold in a cycle.
- SLA note: latency-sensitive endpoints get priority routing; SLA credits available if p95 exceeds target.

Next steps: review and confirm within 3 business days so we can lock pricing and generate a DocuSign for signature. I’ve also added a HubSpot line item (see link) and included the draft term sheet in Drive.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/XYZ-DocuSign-Invite
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/BlueBay-Commerce
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_rate_and_projections

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-optionA-v1.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Kirsten Hall <kirsten@bluebaycommerce.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Samir Patel <samir.p@bluebaycommerce.com>, procurement@bluebaycommerce.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial term sheet (draft) + next steps

Lauren / Team —

We reviewed the draft and are broadly aligned on Option A. Two small asks before signature: 1) can the onboarding credit be increased to 15% if we commit to the 6-month ramp you proposed, and 2) can you confirm whether the 30% Month1 commit can be applied as a soft-commit (i.e., first-month overages billed but offset by credit, not hard cutoffs)? Procurement and I will review the DocuSign when you update the sheet.

If you can send the updated term sheet with those two points changed, we can move to signature this week.

Best,
Kirsten
VP, Product — BlueBay Commerce
